paragraphs: Inflation data turned the Fed from 'probably' to 'almost certainly' hiking in December. October payrolls rose 165,000 (Nov 6) against ~60,000 expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. October CPI (Nov 10) rose 0.4% m/m with core +0.3%, both 0.1pt above forecast; Governor Waller had said hours earlier that a ~0.3% core print should put a 50bp December hike on the table. Futures went to roughly 93-96% odds of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting (vs. ~72-85% at the Nov 2 pull), with a small chance of 50bp. Minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting, released Nov 18, said officials expect further hikes will be needed and flagged AI-related demand as an inflation risk.

Yields gave back the flight-to-safety drop and more. The 10-year fell to ~4.84% on Nov 5 during the equity crash, then rose about 30bp in the week of Nov 9-13 to ~5.15% (FRED), back above the ~4.93% at the Nov 2 pull. The 2-year jumped further, from 4.46% on Nov 5 to 4.88% on Nov 13, so the curve flattened again (10y-2y spread 0.24-0.30 vs. 0.38 on Nov 5). The Fed funds rate is unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.

Equities: the AI selloff became a broad one. After the Nov 3 midterms, Democratic gains raised the prospect of data-center moratoriums, and on Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (worst day since April 2025), the Nasdaq 5.5% and the Dow 3.4%; Nvidia lost 9.3% and AMD 17.3%. Stocks rebounded on Nov 9, then Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thu Nov 12 after reports about his personal conduct, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. The S&P 500 then fell five straight sessions through Nov 18 to 7,323.63, its lowest since late July; the Nasdaq is in a correction, more than 10% below its Oct 6 high. Nvidia's Nov 17 results beat (revenue $115.8B, outlook raised) and the stock rose ~5% after hours, but it closed down 2.9% on Nov 18. That day the Dow fell 1.11% as UnitedHealth dropped 10% on a proposed Medicare anti-fraud audit rule. The VIX closed at 24.63, up from 21.15 on Nov 2. Anthropic's IPO was set to price after the Nov 18 close.

Credit and commodities. HY spreads tightened to 3.20% on Nov 12, then widened back to 3.43% by Nov 17 (FRED), near the 3.44% Oct 30 high; IG is 0.92%. Oil kept falling on U.S.-Iran diplomacy: Brent fell nearly 9% on Nov 4, and on Nov 18 WTI dropped more than 4% to $82.19 and Brent to $90.83 (vs. $96.46 / $104.77 on Nov 2). Gold fell from ~$4,114 on Nov 9 to ~$3,729 on Nov 18 (COMEX front-month) and silver to ~$45 as real yields rose. Data note: FRED's WTI series (89.53 on Nov 17) is again above reported settles, and FRED had not posted Nov 17-18 yields when this was written; the narrative uses reported settles.

The Fed held, but kept a December hike in play. On Oct 28, at Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, the FOMC kept rates at 3.75%-4.00% by a 10-2 vote; Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. Warsh said inflation is too high, that he is 'unwilling and unable' to call financial conditions tight, and that he would not pre-judge meetings. Futures moved to about an 85% chance of a hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting after the press conference (other snapshots put it at ~71-72%), up from ~71% at the Oct 24 pull. The data still runs hot: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualized (vs. 3.1% expected) and September PCE inflation was 3.6% y/y, core 3.1%, in line. The October jobs report is due this week (Fri Nov 6).

Yields fell anyway, on flight to safety. The 10-year rose to ~5.05% on Oct 28 after the presser, then fell to ~4.93% on Oct 30, its lowest close since Sept 9, about 7bp below the Oct 24 pull's ~4.99-5.00%. It fell about 36bp in October, its biggest monthly drop since December 2023. The 2-year fell to ~4.56-4.58%, so the curve steepened.

AI earnings broke tech again, and credit followed. Alphabet fell 12.6% on Oct 29 (its worst day since listing) and Intel ~29% on Oct 30, when the Nasdaq dropped 2.86% and the SOX over 7%. The Nasdaq lost 2.0% on the week and about 5% in October, while the equal-weight S&P 500 rose 4.9% for the month. HY spreads widened to 3.44% and IG to 0.94% on Oct 30 (FRED), both the widest in this dashboard's data. On Mon Nov 2 the Nasdaq fell another 1.07% as Marvell (-13%) and Lumentum (-18%) sank on their $115B merger and Oracle (-8%) announced a $20B stock-and-bond raise; the Dow rose 0.41% and most S&P 500 stocks gained. The VIX closed at 21.15.

Oil reversed hard. WTI closed Oct 30 at $104.12, its highest since mid-September, after gaining more than 15% in October. On Nov 2 Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77 and WTI 7.4% to $96.46 on U.S.-Iran peace-talk hopes and a reported Qatar-brokered plan to reopen Hormuz. That explains Monday's selloff in energy-services stocks and the rally in airlines. Gold fell to ~$3,899 on Oct 30 before recovering to ~$3,957 on Nov 2. Data note: Brent's Oct 30 close is reported as both $117.64 and $113.43, likely the expiring December vs. the January contract; Monday's 7.6% drop matches the $113.43 figure. FRED's Nov 2 yield and spread values had not posted on 11/02/26.

Even after Friday the Dow finished the week +0.41%, the only major index up, so this is a one-day oil/risk-off hit on a week of rotation into the Dow's non-tech names, not a rate shock like the September readings below. The Dow's -1.03% figure on 09/23/26 spans two real sessions compressed into one by the Sept 22 data gap described in the synthesis above. Tuesday Sept 22 the Dow slipped a modest 0.3% while the Nasdaq set a second straight record close - Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin struck a hawkish note ('supply shocks aren't proving short-lived'). Wednesday Sept 23 did the rest of the damage (-0.7%) as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped to roughly 5.11%-5.14% (highest since July 2007) after Fed Governor Michael Barr said 'further policy adjustments are likely to be needed,' and a hotter-than-expected S&P Global composite PMI (58.4 vs. 55.3 forecast) reinforced inflation concerns, pushing October-hike odds to ~66-74%. Same rate/inflation mechanism as the Sept 16 FOMC-day flag below, not a new independent driver. This flag now trips on the day-move threshold rather than the 5-day one, because the FOMC's Sept 16 hike hit in a single session: the Fed hiked 25bp as anticipated, and the Dow fell 631pts (-1.21%) to 51,461.90 on the day — banks led the damage (KBE -2.6%, worst day since February) on fears the hiking cycle continues into 2027. Broad-market and cyclical names have lagged over the past week as rising Treasury yields and oil prices weigh on rate-sensitive and industrial stocks more than mega-cap tech. A hot core CPI print (+0.3% m/m vs +0.2% forecast) raised the odds of a Fed hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting from ~70% to ~90%, and Iran's attacks on commercial/naval vessels in the Middle East have pushed oil higher, adding an inflation and cost headwind for industrials and consumer names that make up a larger share of the Dow than the Nasdaq.
